title: How a Supply Shock Moves Through a Market
production_path_basis: The flagship explanation must remain complete without narration, music, or live data.
audience: General learners and introductory economics students
assumed_knowledge: a model holds some conditions fixed
central_message: A loss of productive capacity shifts supply; with demand initially fixed, the model selects a higher price and lower quantity.
takeaway: A supply-and-demand graph is conditional causal accounting, not an instant forecast or a complete description of an economy.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
scientific_depth: introductory partial-equilibrium supply, demand, curve shifts, equilibrium, adjustment scenarios, and model boundaries
visual_direction: dark analytical dashboard with stable colors for demand, supply, shock, equilibrium, and adjustment paths
pacing: physical hook, baseline model, supply shift, scenario paths, assumptions, synthesis
constraints: distinguish a curve shift from movement along a curve
do not equate one product's price change with economy-wide inflation
make omitted variables and non-instant adjustment visible
success_criteria: baseline equilibrium is P=60 and Q=40
shock equilibrium is P=70 and Q=30
three adjustment paths remain visually distinguishable
assumptions are part of the narrative
all parameters and sampled paths remain editable source
